title: NWP500 external control plan, protocol 1
description: A plan tells the integration's external control feature what state the heater should be in, and when. The feature programs it into the heater's reservation list. Top-level keys are attributes of the intent entity. Rules that span documents or depend on the device (superseded plans, the horizon and the entry budget) are applied by the feature and are listed in docs/external-control-design.md. The $defs named *_attributes, and entry_item, program_item, segment_ack and command_ack, describe what the feature's entities report (spec section 4.2), not the plan.

protocol.description: Protocol version: "1", or "1.x" for a later minor version. "0" and "0.x" are still accepted, and mean the same as 1 (spec section 1.3). Within major version 1 changes are additive (spec section 1.3). A major version the feature does not support rejects the document (unsupported_protocol).

intent_id.description: Unique per plan. The intent entity's state must change on every new plan; use this.

issued_at.description: When the scheduler made the plan, compared at full precision: not truncated. A plan is its intent_id and issued_at (spec section 6.5): a document with the id in force and a later issued_at replaces it; an older document never replaces a newer one (superseded).

segments.description: The timeline, in strictly increasing order of start. Each segment holds until the next segment's start; the last holds until a new plan. An empty list stops the plan: every programmed entry is withdrawn and the heater keeps its state. The first segment names its mode.

commands.description: Protocol 1.3. Device commands, each applied once when the plan is adopted, in order, after its entries are written (spec section 3.7). Only a non-list, an item that is not an object, an item without a valid id, or an id shared with another command or a segment (duplicate_id) rejects the document; a malformed or unknown command is rejected on its own, so this schema describes the commands the feature applies.

command.description: A device command. Any other key is opaque and echoed on the command's acknowledgement, unless it is named as one of the acknowledgement's own keys (id, command, status, reason, warnings, detail).

id.description: Unique in the document, segments' ids included; a shared id rejects the whole document (duplicate_id).

days.description: Days of Vacation, 1 to 99; another value rejects the command (invalid_command).

period_days.description: Days between Anti-Legionella cycles, 1 to 30; another value rejects the command (invalid_command).

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 with a UTC offset. Naive timestamps are rejected. A segment's start is truncated to the minute, when its entry fires; issued_at is kept as given.

mode_name.description: Every mode a reservation entry can set; the adapter applies it as given. An entry has no Vacation: the vacation command sets it. A power_off entry carries the reservation mode 5. The capabilities entity lists these modes.

mode.description: Required on the first segment. A later segment that omits it keeps the previous segment's mode.

reassert.description: Protocol 1.1. Program this segment's entry even when its state repeats the segment before it, so a person's change is ended at its start. An entry that repeats the heater's state starts no recovery.

entry_item.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: one of the feature's own entries, as an item of external_control_last_write's added and removed (spec section 4.2). New keys may be added (spec section 1.3).

kind.description: plan or near_term. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

owner.description: The program's label for the kind: the kind itself.

serves.description: The id of the segment it serves. The same string as plan_next_change's serves.

fires_at.description: The local minute the entry is written for: after any moved_1_min shift, and for a near-term entry its near-term minute. A near-term entry confirmed only after its minute never fired, and is issued again in a later write.

setpoint_raw.description: The setpoint as the device holds it, in half-degrees Celsius.

week.description: The weekday bit of fires_at's local date: Monday 64 to Saturday 2, Sunday 128.

device_entry.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: a reservation entry with the device's keys, as the heater holds it.

program_item.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: an item of plan_fingerprint's entries. A device entry, plus owner. An entry of the feature's own also carries every key of entry_item, except that mode stays the device's mode id, and mode_name holds the mode name. The Reservation Schedule sensor's own mode_name is a display label, not this.

owner.description: foreign (an entry the feature does not own, kept as read), or the owner label of one of the feature's own: plan or near_term.

last_write_attributes.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: external_control_last_write's attributes once a write has been made. Before the first write they are only reason: null.

reason.description: plan, cleanup, near_term or takeover; a write stored by an earlier version may carry another. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

added.description: The entries the write added; null when truncated.

removed.description: The entries the write removed; null when truncated, which drops removed before added.

truncated.description: True when a list is null because the attributes would exceed the recorder's 16 KiB limit, which would keep none of them. The counts are always given.

confirmed.description: For the whole write: true once the device read back the list sent; false from the first unconfirmed attempt (the retry may still confirm it), or for a live write that could not be sent; null for a simulated write (shadow).

simulated.description: True for a write made in shadow, which was not sent.

override_report.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: a person's removal of one of the plan's entries, on plan_entry_removed (spec section 4.2). One report per key: field; for removed, field, segment and value's kind.

field.description: removed. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

override_attributes.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: plan_entry_removed's attributes. The latest report's keys at the top level, and every report in force. Off, no report is in force: the report keys are null, reports is empty and report_count is 0.

reports.description: Every report in force, oldest first, less any left out by truncated.

truncated.description: True when the oldest reports are left out of reports to stay within the recorder's 16 KiB limit. report_count counts them all.

ack_attributes.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: plan_status's attributes (spec section 4.2). The entity's state is none, rejected, shadow, pending, partly_programmed or programmed.

intent_id.description: The plan in force's, or, with none in force, the rejected document's.

reason.description: Set only in the rejected state: why the document was rejected whole (section 3.5).

detail.description: Set only in the rejected state: a readable explanation.

segments.description: The plan in force's segments, in its order; empty in the rejected state.

commands.description: Protocol 1.3. The plan in force's device commands, in its order (section 3.7).

rejected.description: The most recent document rejected whole, or null. Cleared when a document received after it is accepted.

segment_ack.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: one segment on plan_status (spec section 4.2), with the segment's opaque keys.

status.description: shadow, scheduled, pending, programmed, merged, in_force, ended, failed or removed. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

reason.description: beyond_horizon, entry_budget, write_not_confirmed, or not_applied_on_device. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

warnings.description: moved_1_min. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

fires_at.description: The minute its entry fires, or will fire once programmed; null if it has none.

command_ack.description: Entity attributes, not part of a plan: one device command on plan_status (spec sections 3.7 and 4.2), with the command's opaque keys, which never include its own keys' names. A command that is not supported has its other keys echoed as opaque.

command.description: As sent, an unsupported one included; empty if the item gave none that is a string.

status.description: shadow, pending, applied, failed or rejected. It reports the application only: a person's later change does not change it. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

reason.description: failed: write_not_confirmed or not_applied_on_device; rejected: invalid_command or unsupported_command; otherwise null. Treat a value you do not know as opaque.

detail.description: A readable explanation, given when rejected, and when failed with write_not_confirmed: the library's message.

reported_time.description: A time the feature reports: ISO 8601 with a UTC offset.

capabilities_attributes.description: The capabilities entity's attributes; its state is version. What runs, the entry budget, and what a plan may say. Protocol 1.4 adds modes, setpoint and commands.

protocol_versions.description: The newest minor version implemented of each major, in the order of protocols.

mode.description: live writes the heater's list; shadow plans and reports without writing.

setpoint_resolution_c.description: Setpoints are held in half degrees Celsius.

horizon_h.description: How far ahead an entry is programmed, in hours.

near_term_lead_min.description: How far ahead a change needed now is written as an entry, in minutes.

entry_limit.description: The size of the list the feature writes.

entry_reserve.description: Entries kept free of the plan's.

entries_available.description: Entries the plan may still use now; null until the heater's list is read. It changes as entries fire, and is left out of version.

modes.description: Protocol 1.4. The modes a segment may name.

setpoint.description: Protocol 1.4. The heater's own setpoint range, inclusive. A segment's setpoint is checked after rounding to half degrees Celsius (150 °F is 65.5 °C, the 149.9 °F maximum); one outside the range rejects the plan (setpoint_out_of_range). Null until the heater's features are read, and plans are not range-checked meanwhile.

commands.description: Protocol 1.4. Each command the feature applies, by name: its keys, their types, and whole numbers' inclusive ranges.

version.description: A hash of the declaration, entries_available left out; it changes whenever the declaration does.

intent_attributes.description: The intent entity's attributes; its state is the plan in force's intent_id, or none. The plan's opaque top-level keys are echoed.

program_hash_attributes.description: The program hash entity's attributes; its state is the hash of the list the feature wants on the heater, comparable with the reservation schedule sensor's, and unknown until the list is read.

programmed_until_attributes.description: The programmed-until entity's attributes; its state is the first segment not programmed, or the last once all are.

complete.description: Whether every segment is programmed; null with no plan.

scheduled.description: Entries waiting for room in the list or within the horizon.

next_entry_attributes.description: The next entry entity's attributes; its state is when the feature's next entry fires.

wanted_setpoint_attributes.description: The wanted setpoint entity's attributes; its state is the setpoint the plan wants now, in Home Assistant's unit.

segment.description: The segment in force, as the ack's in_force; null when none is, or a person removed its entry.

heartbeat_attributes.description: The heartbeat entity's attributes; its state is updated at least every 15 minutes while the feature runs.

started_at.description: When the feature last started: a change means a reload.

in_sync_attributes.description: The heater-matches-plan entity's attributes; it is on when the heater's list hashes as the program does, unknown until the list is read.
